title: 9 One-Person Businesses With More Demand Than Competition
promo_conflict: Host sells remote cleaning business coaching and ranks it #1.

idea.name: Portable toilet rental and servicing
idea.one_liner: Rent porta-potties to construction sites (6-18 month contracts, monthly per-unit billing plus weekly pump-outs) and to weddings/festivals for weekends

key_quotes.quote: Now, every active construction site is legally required to have sanitation on site for the entire length of the build.
So, when you land construction contracts, those will run you depending on the size of the building 6 to 18 months and you get to bill a monthly per unit

uk_legal_risk.reason: Collecting and disposing of toilet waste requires an Environment Agency waste carrier registration and licensed disposal

stated_problem.quote: it's that almost nobody does it as a real business with fast turnaround, with, you know, an actual shop you can pull up to, drop your machines off,
stated_problem.speaker: Johnny

idea.name: Small engine repair shop for contractors
idea.one_liner: Professional fast-turnaround repair of mowers, generators, chainsaws and pressure washers for landscapers and service contractors
idea.customer: landscaping and home service contractors, households

key_quotes.quote: Now, this can print a ton of money per hour and I don't see many people talking about this one on the internet and certainly nobody under 50 is doing it.

idea.name: Fire extinguisher inspection route
idea.one_liner: Build a route of commercial accounts for legally mandated annual extinguisher inspection and tagging in a fragmented market

key_quotes.quote: Fire marshals will check for that tag, and that makes it one of the few like home service style businesses where the lot self is doing your sales pitch for you.
And then, slowly over time as you build up a route of a few hundred accounts, you're going to start to add some serious recurring revenue.

claims.quote: There's a ton of fire inspection businesses that do millions and tens of millions a year.

ideas.other_uk_rules: Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005; BS 5306-3 servicing by competent person (BAFE SP101)

stated_problem.quote: So, when a bay goes down, that warehouse can't load or unload trucks.
stated_problem.speaker: Johnny

idea.name: Commercial dock and door equipment service
idea.one_liner: Repair and preventive maintenance of dock levellers, roller doors and seals for warehouses on quarterly contracts plus premium emergency calls
idea.revenue_model: quarterly service plans and emergency call-outs

key_quotes.quote: Now, let's say you land 20 warehouse accounts on a quarterly service plan at call it a few hundred bucks a visit,

idea.name: Waste oil and grease collection route
idea.one_liner: Recurring pickup of used motor oil and fryer grease from auto shops and restaurants, charging a pickup fee and selling the oil to re-refiners

key_quotes.quote: You sign accounts to a recurring pickup schedule and once you're their hauler of record, they're no longer shopping around.
But on top of this, you can also take that oil and sell it to re-refiners. Right?

uk_legal_risk.reason: Waste oil is hazardous waste; requires waste carrier registration, consignment notes and EA permits

stated_problem.quote: carriers lose about $4,000 a month per truck that's not on the road simply because they can't find qualified drivers.
stated_problem.speaker: Johnny

idea.name: Truck driver recruiting/placement
idea.one_liner: Run Facebook ads to CDL holders, vet them, and place qualified drivers with carriers for a placement fee
idea.revenue_model: placement fee up to $4,000 per hire

key_quotes.quote: And that's why they'll pay a placement fee of up to $4,000 for every qualified driver you bring them who gets hired and stays on.
All you need to learn how to do is run Facebook ads targeting CDL holders and owner-operators who are looking for better freight

claims.quote: And if you place 10 qualified drivers a month even at half the top, you know, of what someone's willing to pay, I mean, you're looking at about like what, 20 grand a month?

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook recruiting ads to CDL holders

ideas.other_uk_rules: Conduct of Employment Agencies Regulations 2003 (no fees to workers); UK GDPR for candidate data; HGV licence/CPC checks

stated_problem.quote: because millions of people need a ride to dialysis, chemo, uh medical random medical appointments and they just simply cannot drive themselves
stated_problem.speaker: Johnny

idea.name: Non-emergency medical transportation dispatch
idea.one_liner: Coordinate recurring rides to dialysis/chemo using independent drivers, handling scheduling and Medicaid/insurance billing

key_quotes.quote: Well, let's say a dialysis patient needs a ride three times a week every week for years.
And you can handle all of the scheduling, the insurance billing, the compliance, and route the ride straight to them.

uk_legal_risk.reason: UK non-emergency patient transport is NHS-commissioned and CQC-regulated; carrying passengers for hire needs private hire/PSV licensing

idea.name: Foundation repair and waterproofing lead-gen/brokerage
idea.one_liner: Market and sell foundation/waterproofing jobs ($5-15k) via Google Business Profile, then subcontract to licensed crews and keep a cut
idea.customer: homeowners with cracked foundations or wet basements

key_quotes.quote: You partner with licensed foundation waterproofing crews who already own all of that specialized equipment.
So, you know, a Google Business Profile, some before-and-after photos, and then just being by the phone when someone calls is going to put you ahead of a lot of people

claims.quote: And jobs commonly run between 5 to 15,000 dollars because the alternative is a house that keeps getting worse,

ideas.other_uk_rules: Consumer Contracts Regulations cancellation rights for doorstep/off-premises contracts

stated_problem.quote: Most of whom don't answer their phone, don't have a website, and don't really want to grow or take the time to learn the skill of marketing, sales, and recruiting.
stated_problem.speaker: Johnny

idea.name: Remote-run house cleaning business with independent cleaners
idea.one_liner: Owner handles marketing, booking and recruiting from a laptop while independent cleaners do jobs for a 50% split; ~1 in 3 one-time cleans convert to recurring

key_quotes.quote: This is the one that separates it from, let's say, foundation repair because roughly one in every three one-time cleanings will convert to a recurring client,
You pay them 50%, you keep 50%, it's a win-win business.

claims.quote: Now, if we run some quick numbers, your first time deep clean's going to go for about, call it, $350.
so you really only need 30 cleans to get to about 10 grand a month in revenue, or three to four grand in in profit with absolutely zero employees.

uk_legal_risk.reason: Treating controlled cleaners as self-employed risks worker-status claims (holiday pay, NMW) post Uber v Aslam
